newsitem.title: USA: Ford UAW workers see gains under new pact.
newsitem.headline: Ford UAW workers see gains under new pact.

text.p: The United Auto Workers said Wednesday that its tentative three-year wage agreement with Ford Motor Co will provide economic gains of more than $13,900 for a typical worker over the life of the contract.

In an outline of the new pact distributed to members of the UAW's National Ford Council, the union said monthly pension payments will increase by $265 for workers who retire after 30 years of service before age 62.
The tentative agreement covering about 105,000 UAW members at Ford was reached Monday.

Taking into account the $265 increase, monthly pension benefits for workers who retire during the new contract will be $2,295 after October 1, 1998, a 13 percent increase from the $2,030 paid under the previous contract.

The three-year deal calls for union members to receive a lump sum payment of $2,000 in the first year. Workers will get three percent base wage increases in the second and third years of the agreement.
Workers will get an annual Christmas bonus of up to $600 each under the deal.
The base wage for assembly workers will be $21.60 an hour at the end of the new contract, versus $17.945 at the end of the old contract.
Including a cost-of-living-adjustment "fold-in" payment that adds $1.03 an hour, the base assembly worker wage is $18.975 at the start of the new contract.
UAW Ford workers will receive a total of 48 paid holidays under the new three-year agreement, including a newly negotiated holiday on Veterans Day November 13, 1998.

Including all wage gains, bonuses and cost-of-living adjustments and other payments, the typical Ford UAW worker's total cash compensation will increase by about $13,910 over the life of the new agreement.

Under the new contract, workers retain their fully paid health care benefits and receive several improvements in coverage. The annual maximum dental benefit increases to $1,400 per worker from $1,200 currently.
Workers also receive new coverage for prostate cancer tests and increased benefits for vision and selected medical devices.

The union said it rejected company attempts to force workers to pay part of their health insurance premiums and restrict health care providers they can see. Prescription drug co-payments for Michigan workers increased to $5 from $2.50.
